Earlier records call it *the runtime* or *the simulation runtime*; `simulator` is the canonical name, adopted 2026-08-03 when the simulator effort began.
   106	
   107	## Production monitoring
   108	
   109	**monitoring source** — a project-owned source of production calls from an agent platform. It holds what egma needs to find and import calls from the selected production targets.
   110	
   111	**monitoring import failure** — one production call that a monitoring source could not import after its allowed attempts. It remains visible so a user can inspect the failure and retry the import.
   112	
   113	## What a simulation produces
   114	
   115	**transcript** — the record of the conversation. Turns, each labelled `human:` or `agent:`, with timings, audio references, and the agent's tool calls — with results where egma observed them, and each call marked when a mock tool answered it or when egma refused it. A call carrying neither mark is one egma never stood in the path of: three shapes, three histories.
   116	
   117	**outcome** — Anthropic's *"the final state in the environment"*. Explicitly **not** what the agent said. A voice agent that says *"you're all set for Tuesday"* while the booking silently failed has a good transcript and a bad outcome, and a transcript-only grader passes it. That is the failure trust dies on.
   118	
   119	Populated from observed tool calls where the connection exposes them. Customer-registered verification hooks — egma calling the customer's API after the call to check the booking exists — are designed for, not built on the first-simulation path.
   120	
   121	> **The clearest open slot in the market.** Nine of ten voice-testing vendors verify only the agent's words and its self-reported tool calls. Only Coval queries external state.
   122	
   123	**metric** — something **measured**, not judged: duration, turn count, latency percentiles, interruption count, tool-call count, cost. **Derived from the trace's spans by one shared measure module** — the same computation serves the metrics display and the graders, for simulations and production traces alike, so the number on screen and the number judged can never disagree. (Previously *emitted by the runtime*; re-homed to spans 2026-08-14, grader-redesign grilling — the simulator's duty is emitting honest span timings.) Never an entity, never attached to a test.
   124	
   125	**measure catalog** — the documented, versioned list of the measures egma computes from spans, each with its span-level definition, so that a grader reading a metric names a known measure rather than guessing a string — and so the metric dropdown **Use** shows has a source of truth. A contract, not a table. Added 2026-08-07, grading grilling; extended to pin span-level definitions 2026-08-14.
   126	
   127	## Monitoring
   128	
   129	**monitoring** — the product surface where a team reads its production traffic: the navigation **group** and the **Transcripts** item under it — the group label carries the word, and the item says what its page is (regrouped 2026-08-19, product-UI ticket 17). It shows production traces only — a simulation is read under the run that produced it, so the two kinds of traffic have two surfaces over the one store. A UI word: `trace` and `span` stay storage words that never reach a screen, and the page word for one conversation remains *transcript*. Settled 2026-08-16, monitoring grilling.
   130	
   131	**telemetry** — what egma reports about *itself*: the containers' logs and request spans, the pages' analytics and errors, the box's vitals. Never a customer's data and never in ClickHouse — `trace` and `span` stay conversation words, and egma's own telemetry never shares the trace store's pipe. Behind one flag, `EGMA_TELEMETRY`, off by default everywhere; hosted egma turns it on and points it at PostHog and CloudWatch. Added 2026-08-17, observability effort; see [ADR-0010](docs/adr/0010-egmas-own-telemetry.md).
   132	
   133	## Judging
   134	
   135	**grader** — a running copy of a grader-library entry: the row that judges, and the thing verdict rows name. Created by pressing **Use** on a library entry, or seeded at project creation. It points at its entry (`library_id` — the connecting tissue, never null, never orphaned: deleting a referenced entry is refused), carries the entry's `type`, and holds its **filled-in values** — latency's `[{metric, bound}]` — in immutable versions; editing the values mints the next version, and a run pins the versions it executed. Each grader version also points at one immutable grader-library definition version. The prompt or code is shared once at the library layer, never copied into each project, while the exact definition used by an old run stays reconstructable. Redefined 2026-08-19, model-execution cutover; the word previously named the authored logic itself.
   136	
   137	**The distinction that matters: a metric measures, a grader judges.** Nobody wrote down that the call took four minutes — it just happened. Someone had to decide that verifying identity before disclosing a balance matters, and write the criteria. That's the line.
   138	
   139	They connect in one direction: **a grader may read a metric.** *"Fail if p90 response time exceeds 2 seconds"* is a grader whose input is a measurement. So latency is always known, and only becomes a verdict if you ask for one.
   140	
   141	A grader declares:
   142	
   143	- **required** — `true` (default): the test cannot pass unless this copy fully passes. `false`: a **diagnostic** — judged, displayed with its fraction, never able to fail anything. τ2-bench's outside-the-reward-basis components, and the only loudness switch v0 has. Replaces the P0/P1/P2 priority ladder, retired 2026-08-14, grader-redesign grilling.
   144	- **its scope** — the whole answer to where the copy applies: two switches — **judges simulations** (default on) and **judges production** (default off, with the production sampling rate) — and a **filter** under each switch. `both` retired 2026-08-20, grader-scope grilling: it was two switches written as one word, and the one word hid the two opposite safe defaults (simulations exist to be judged; production judging spends money on traffic nobody asked egma to create). Dormant is **no copy at all** — the switches say where an existing copy applies, not whether it exists; pressing Use is still the enabling and deleting the copy is the off-switch.
   145	- **which modalities it can score** (declared by its library entry). *"Didn't interrupt the caller"* is meaningless on chat. A grader that can't score the modality is **skipped**, and the results view must say *skipped*, not *failed*.
   146	
   147	**grader library** — the shelf of grader definitions: `grader_library` holds each stable library identity and immutable definition versions hold its executable prompt, output definition, parameter schema, or code. An entry declares its **type** — `llm_as_judge` or `code`; reserved: `human`, `ml_model`, `external`. **Owner derives from tenancy**: null organization and project means egma owns the entry — the one deliberate exception to hard-required tenancy — seeded from a catalog in egma's code. When an Egma release changes a definition, reconciliation mints one new shared definition version and new grader versions for active running copies. New runs pin those versions; old runs keep the old definition through their already-pinned grader versions. No definition is copied per project, and no catalog edit changes the meaning of an old verdict. Team-authored entries land in the same library with tenancy set, when custom authoring arrives. Redefined 2026-08-19, model-execution cutover.
   148	
   149	**predefined grader** — a library entry egma owns and ships. v0 ships two: **expected_behaviors** (`llm_as_judge`) and **latency** (`code`). Replaces *built-in grader*, 2026-08-14 — `predefined` is the word users arrive with (Cekura), the persona lesson applied the cheap way again.
   150	
   151	**rubric** — the criteria text an `llm_as_judge` grader carries. Anthropic's word. Added 2026-08-07; repointed from the retired `llm_rubric` type, 2026-08-14.
   152	
   153	**assertion** — one 0-or-1 check inside a grader. A grader holds one or more assertions, and each is judged in isolation: for an LLM-judged grader, one independent judge call per assertion — Anthropic's per-dimension isolation, which is how the engine has run since the grading effort. The expected-behaviors grader's assertions are the test's own expected behaviors; a code grader's assertions are the entries in its configuration. Un-banned and adopted 2026-08-14, grader-redesign grilling: the word once banned as a synonym for a whole grader now names the level below it, and the old ban stands exactly there — an assertion is never a grader. One word at every layer: the verdict store's column is `assertion` too (renamed from `dimension` by the same grilling — the store is pre-launch and small, so the rename is cheap).
   154	
   155	**Applicability: a running copy applies to everything its switches and filters allow.** There is still no per-test attachment — the `test_grader` junction stays dropped, and a test names no graders; narrowing is declared grader-side, so a check written once judges everything it covers without anyone remembering to attach it. A copy whose switch or filter excludes a conversation writes no verdict rows at all — absent, never `skipped`, which keeps meaning "applied but could not score the modality". Settled 2026-08-20, grader-scope grilling: the filters deferred by the grader-redesign spec arrived, per side — see the grader-scope spec. **Never attached to a suite** stands untouched.
   156	
   157	**filter** — the where/and rows under one switch of a running copy's scope: `{fact, any_of | none_of, values}`, rows joined by AND, at most one row per fact, values inside a row OR'd; empty means everything that switch allows. Facts come from a **fact catalog** in egma's code that declares each fact's value source, its operators, and which sides can answer it — `agent` on both sides, `test` on simulations only in v1 — so the production builder never offers a fact a live call cannot answer, and an unanswerable rule is unrepresentable rather than refused. A filter is live and unversioned, like the switches: what a grader judges by is versioned; where it applies is not. Added 2026-08-20, grader-scope grilling.
   158	
   159	**scope_editable** — on the library entry: whether copies of it may re-aim their scope. Using an egma-defined grader means using it **as is** — you edit what egma allows; false locks the whole scope (switches, rate, both filters) on every copy, seeded or Use-created. expected_behaviors ships locked (judges simulations on, production off, no filter), which also enforces that it can never judge a live call — a production trace has no test to judge against; latency ships editable. `required` is not scope — how loudly, not where — and stays editable on locked copies. Forking a grader is not a v1 concept. Added 2026-08-20, grader-scope grilling.
   160	
   161	**expected-behaviors grader** — the predefined `llm_as_judge` entry that judges a simulation against its test's expected behaviors. Its assertions are the test's own sentences — supplied per test at judging time, one isolated judge call each ([ADR-0007](docs/adr/0007-grading-runs-in-its-own-service.md)) — so the entry itself defines no assertions and **Use** asks nothing. In the library like any entry, and **auto-seeded as an active running copy in every new project** (judges simulations only, required, locked as-is by its entry's `scope_editable: false`), so a first run is judged with zero setup. Structurally simulations-only: a production trace has no test, and the locked scope is what enforces it. Supersedes ADR-0004's never-a-row clause — see [ADR-0009](docs/adr/0009-grader-library-and-running-copies.md); falsifiability still lives on the behaviors list, required non-empty at write time, exactly as ADR-0004 placed it.
   162	
   163	**verdict** — `passed`, `failed`, `skipped`, or `errored`, written **one row per assertion**. `skipped` and `errored` are load-bearing and must never be collapsed into `failed`: a test that couldn't run is not a test that failed, and a check that couldn't read its inputs didn't fail either.    164	
   165	## The onboarding surface
   166	
   167	**wizard** — the complete terminal experience `npx egma` presents when run bare: its UI, the intelligent work performed by the developer's local coding agent, and the deterministic work performed through the same CLI modules as the headless verbs. Clarified 2026-08-09 during the self-hosted phone onboarding grilling; originally added 2026-08-06 ([ADR-0006](docs/adr/0006-onboarding-wizard-drives-the-customers-coding-agent.md)).
   168	
   169	**egma folder** — the `egma/` directory in the customer's repo: project, agent, and connection config; one directory per test suite under `tests/`; a `suite.yaml` carrying that suite's stable ID and mutable name; one markdown file per test inside its suite directory; and one file for the project's mock tools. The folder is committed, never gitignored; nothing secret ever lands in it. The platform remains the store of record — the folder is a working copy.
   170	
   171	**platform binding** — the non-secret platform URL written in `egma/config.yaml` beside the resource identifiers that platform owns. It chooses the platform that receives those identifiers; credentials and a platform-instance identity are never part of the binding. An unbound repository uses hosted egma at `app.egma.ai`. See [ADR-0012](docs/adr/0012-agent-repositories-bind-to-a-platform-url.md).
   172	
   173	**pull / push** — the explicit sync verbs between the egma folder and the platform, on git's model: `pull` writes the platform's current versions into files; `push` uploads and **refuses** when the platform has moved since the last pull. **That refusal is a property of versioned things**: a test earns it, and so do the mock-tool overrides that version with it.    174	
   175	## Banned words
   176	
   177	Do not use these — in code, schema, API, docs or UI.
   178	
   179	| Don't use | Why | Use |
   180	|---|---|---|
   181	| `eval`, `evaluation` | Everyone says it, nobody agrees what it points at | nothing — informal prose only |
   182	| `evaluator` | Half the industry means the test, the other half the thing scoring it | `grader` |
   183	| `scorer`, `check` | Borrowed words for the judging job — one word per level | `grader` for the authored logic, `assertion` for one criterion inside it |
   184	| `dimension` | The verdict store's old column name for it — one entity, one word, at every layer including storage | `assertion` |
   185	| `gate` | Considered for the must-pass flag during the grader redesign, not chosen | `required` |
   186	| `built-in grader` | Renamed 2026-08-14 — `predefined` is the word users arrive with (Cekura) | `predefined grader` |
   187	| `metric` *for scoring logic* | A metric measures, a grader judges | `grader` |
   188	| `digital human` | The old name, renamed 2026-08-05 — one entity, one word | `persona` |
   189	| `simulant`, `virtual human`, `synthetic user`, `digital twin` | Considered, not chosen | `persona` |
   190	| `scenario` *as an entity* | It's what a test says, not a thing of its own | a field on `test` |
   191	| `session` *for a conversation* | Same thing as a simulation | `simulation` |
   192	| `trial`, `attempt`, `iteration` | Running a test twice just makes two simulations | `simulation` |
   193	| `call` | Half of them are chats | `simulation` |
   194	| `conversation` | Same thing as a simulation | `simulation` |
   195	| `caller` | Breaks the moment it's a chat | `persona` |
   196	| `result` *as an entity* | A result is "passed" or "failed" — it isn't the recording | `verdict`, or the simulation itself |
   197	| `experiment`, `batch` | Borrowed from a different world | `run` |
   198	| `expected outcome` *as a test field* | Replaced 2026-08-05 — the test's expectations are a list of behaviors, not one paragraph of end state | `expected behaviors` |
   199	| `tool mock` | The inverted form of the entity's name — one entity, one word | `mock tool` |
   200	| `stub`, `fake` *for a mock tool* | Same job, one word | `mock tool` |
   201	
   202	**One carve-out, and it is not a loophole.** `session` **is the right word for a signed-in browser session**, and the ban does not reach it. The auth provider owns a `session` table, the provider seam's fourth method is `revokeSession`, and [ADR-0001](docs/adr/0001-auth-provider-owns-identity-only.md) and the control-plane spec both require the word in that sense — so the unqualified ban forbade what the decision records mandate, which is how a glossary stops being consulted. The ban stands exactly where it was aimed: **`session` never names a conversation.** A simulation is a simulation.
   203	
   204	The same carve-out covers one more seam, for the same reason: **the Agent Client Protocol names its connection to a driven coding agent a `session`** (`session/new`, `session/prompt`, `session/request_permission` are the wire methods), and [ADR-0006](docs/adr/0006-onboarding-wizard-drives-the-customers-coding-agent.md) mandates that SDK — so the CLI's ACP seam uses the protocol's word as-is, exactly as the auth seam uses the provider's.    207	
   208	Good words. Each means exactly one thing and is never borrowed for another.

   213	| `customer` | the organization paying for egma | the persona |

   167	**wizard** — the complete terminal experience `npx egma` presents when run bare: its UI, the intelligent work performed by the developer's local coding agent, and the deterministic work performed through the same CLI modules as the headless verbs.    169	**egma folder** — the `egma/` directory in the customer's repo: project, agent, and connection config; one directory per test suite under `tests/`; a `suite.yaml` carrying that suite's stable ID and mutable name; one markdown file per test inside its suite directory; and one file for the project's mock tools.    170	
   171	**platform binding** — the non-secret platform URL written in `egma/config.yaml` beside the resource identifiers that platform owns. See [ADR-0012](docs/adr/0012-agent-repositories-bind-to-a-platform-url.md).
   172	
   173	**pull / push** — the explicit sync verbs between the egma folder and the platform, on git's model: `pull` writes the platform's current versions into files; `push` uploads and **refuses** when the platform has moved since the last pull. **That refusal is a property of versioned things**: a test earns it, and so do the mock-tool overrides that version with it.    175	## Banned words
   176	
   177	Do not use these — in code, schema, API, docs or UI.
   178	
   179	| Don't use | Why | Use |
   180	|---|---|---|

   182	| `evaluator` | Half the industry means the test, the other half the thing scoring it | `grader` |
   183	| `scorer`, `check` | Borrowed words for the judging job — one word per level | `grader` for the authored logic, `assertion` for one criterion inside it |
   184	| `dimension` | The verdict store's old column name for it — one entity, one word, at every layer including storage | `assertion` |
   185	| `gate` | Considered for the must-pass flag during the grader redesign, not chosen | `required` |
   186	| `built-in grader` | Renamed 2026-08-14 — `predefined` is the word users arrive with (Cekura) | `predefined grader` |
   187	| `metric` *for scoring logic* | A metric measures, a grader judges | `grader` |
   188	| `digital human` | The old name, renamed 2026-08-05 — one entity, one word | `persona` |
   189	| `simulant`, `virtual human`, `synthetic user`, `digital twin` | Considered, not chosen | `persona` |
   190	| `scenario` *as an entity* | It's what a test says, not a thing of its own | a field on `test` |
   191	| `session` *for a conversation* | Same thing as a simulation | `simulation` |
   192	| `trial`, `attempt`, `iteration` | Running a test twice just makes two simulations | `simulation` |
   193	| `call` | Half of them are chats | `simulation` |
   194	| `conversation` | Same thing as a simulation | `simulation` |
   195	| `caller` | Breaks the moment it's a chat | `persona` |
   196	| `result` *as an entity* | A result is "passed" or "failed" — it isn't the recording | `verdict`, or the simulation itself |
   197	| `experiment`, `batch` | Borrowed from a different world | `run` |
   198	| `expected outcome` *as a test field* | Replaced 2026-08-05 — the test's expectations are a list of behaviors, not one paragraph of end state | `expected behaviors` |
   199	| `tool mock` | The inverted form of the entity's name — one entity, one word | `mock tool` |
   200	| `stub`, `fake` *for a mock tool* | Same job, one word | `mock tool` |
   201	
   202	**One carve-out, and it is not a loophole.** `session` **is the right word for a signed-in browser session**, and the ban does not reach it.    203	
   204	The same carve-out covers one more seam, for the same reason: **the Agent Client Protocol names its connection to a driven coding agent a `session`** (`session/new`, `session/prompt`, `session/request_permission` are the wire methods), and [ADR-0006](docs/adr/0006-onboarding-wizard-drives-the-customers-coding-agent.md) mandates that SDK — so the CLI's ACP seam uses the protocol's word as-is, exactly as the auth seam uses the provider's.    206	## Reserved words
   207	
   208	Good words. Each means exactly one thing and is never borrowed for another.
   209	
   210	| Word | Always means | Never means |
   211	|---|---|---|
   212	| `user` | the developer using egma | the persona |
   213	| `customer` | the organization paying for egma | the persona |
   214	| `agent` | the voice agent under test | egma's side of the call |
   215	| `human` | the caller's side of a transcript | a real person reviewing results |
   216	| `project` | the tenancy container below the organization | any resource inside one — LangSmith's collision, where "project" is a resource four levels beneath a "workspace" container |
   217	| `trace` | one conversation end to end, simulated or real — a storage-layer word that never appears in a UI | a UI-facing name for a simulation |
   218	| `span` | one timed thing inside a trace — a storage-layer word that never appears in a UI | a turn specifically; a turn is one kind of span |
   219	
   220	`trace` and `span` were put on this list by [The unified ClickHouse trace schema](.scratch/first-simulation-path/issues/09-unified-clickhouse-trace-schema.md), which needed a word for a conversation that might not be a simulation: a production trace has no test, no run and no persona, so `simulation` cannot name it.    221	
   222	`global` was briefly the label over the standing pair (Agents, Graders), added 2026-08-19 by [17 — Group the navigation](.scratch/product-ui/issues/17-group-navigation-under-global-simulations-and-monitoring.md) with its objection recorded: nothing under it was global, and a reader could predict organization-wide settings behind the word. The word is free again and means nothing in this product.
   223	
   224	## Mapping to Anthropic's taxonomy
   225	
   226	| Anthropic | egma | Note |
   227	|---|---|---|
   228	| evaluation suite | **test suite** | egma's is a named container, not a saved selector or execution plan |
   229	| task | **test** | |
   230	| trial | **simulation** | |
   231	| *(unnamed)* | **run** | Anthropic leaves this slot empty; 8 of 10 voice vendors call it a run |
   232	| transcript / trajectory | **transcript** | |
   233	| outcome | **outcome** | |
   234	| grader | **grader** | |
   235	| assertion (sometimes called checks) | **assertion** | Same word; one 0-or-1 check inside a grader |
   236	| tracked metrics | **metric** | A field, not an entity |
   237	| agent harness | **agent** + **connection** | Split, because reaching the agent is a first-class problem in voice |
   238	| *(none)* | **persona** | Anthropic's taxonomy has one agent; a voice conversation has two participants |
   239	
   240	## Deferred
   241	
   242	Named here so the boundary is clear; decided elsewhere.
   243	
   244	- **What a grader is made of** was settled 2026-08-07 by the grading effort (`.scratch/grading/spec.md`) and **re-settled 2026-08-14 by the grader redesign** (`.scratch/grader-redesign/spec.md`): a library of definitions, running copies, assertions, binary scoring. Where the two disagree, the redesign wins.
   245	- **Thresholds, weights, filters, custom authoring, human corrections, the `ml_model` and `external` types, and any warn tier** — each designed with a named home and deferred, in the grader-redesign spec's future-work section. Deliberately not sketched anywhere else, so the sketch cannot fork.
   246	- **Classification** — labels that segment without judging: sentiment, topic of a conversation, where it dropped off. A third concept beside measure (a number, automatic) and grader (a verdict, chosen): a label, chosen. Every surveyed vendor ships it; none names it. Deliberately deferred so labels are never wedged into verdicts.
   247	- **Whether a persona behaves like a real caller**, and how egma would claim it does, is not yet specified. It is the credibility floor of the product.
   248	- **Where personas come from.** Research strongly favours grounding them in the customer's own recordings over describing them from demographics.
   249	- **Chain-consistent mock worlds** — bundles that keep `lookup_user` → account → booking data coherent across mock tools (the "John Smith world").    155	**Applicability: a running copy applies to everything its switches and filters allow.** There is still no per-test attachment — the `test_grader` junction stays dropped, and a test names no graders; narrowing is declared grader-side, so a check written once judges everything it covers without anyone remembering to attach it. A copy whose switch or filter excludes a conversation writes no verdict rows at all — absent, never `skipped`, which keeps meaning "applied but could not score the modality". Settled 2026-08-20, grader-scope grilling: the filters deferred by the grader-redesign spec arrived, per side — see the grader-scope spec. **Never attached to a suite** stands untouched.
   156	
   157	**filter** — the where/and rows under one switch of a running copy's scope: `{fact, any_of | none_of, values}`, rows joined by AND, at most one row per fact, values inside a row OR'd; empty means everything that switch allows. Facts come from a **fact catalog** in egma's code that declares each fact's value source, its operators, and which sides can answer it — `agent` on both sides, `test` on simulations only in v1 — so the production builder never offers a fact a live call cannot answer, and an unanswerable rule is unrepresentable rather than refused. A filter is live and unversioned, like the switches: what a grader judges by is versioned; where it applies is not. Added 2026-08-20, grader-scope grilling.
   158	
   159	**scope_editable** — on the library entry: whether copies of it may re-aim their scope. Using an egma-defined grader means using it **as is** — you edit what egma allows; false locks the whole scope (switches, rate, both filters) on every copy, seeded or Use-created. expected_behaviors ships locked (judges simulations on, production off, no filter), which also enforces that it can never judge a live call — a production trace has no test to judge against; latency ships editable. `required` is not scope — how loudly, not where — and stays editable on locked copies. Forking a grader is not a v1 concept. Added 2026-08-20, grader-scope grilling.
   160	
   161	**expected-behaviors grader** — the predefined `llm_as_judge` entry that judges a simulation against its test's expected behaviors. Its assertions are the test's own sentences — supplied per test at judging time, one isolated judge call each ([ADR-0007](docs/adr/0007-grading-runs-in-its-own-service.md)) — so the entry itself defines no assertions and **Use** asks nothing. In the library like any entry, and **auto-seeded as an active running copy in every new project** (judges simulations only, required, locked as-is by its entry's `scope_editable: false`), so a first run is judged with zero setup. Structurally simulations-only: a production trace has no test, and the locked scope is what enforces it. Supersedes ADR-0004's never-a-row clause — see [ADR-0009](docs/adr/0009-grader-library-and-running-copies.md); falsifiability still lives on the behaviors list, required non-empty at write time, exactly as ADR-0004 placed it.
   162	
   163	**verdict** — `passed`, `failed`, `skipped`, or `errored`, written **one row per assertion**. `skipped` and `errored` are load-bearing and must never be collapsed into `failed`: a test that couldn't run is not a test that failed, and a check that couldn't read its inputs didn't fail either. A verdict row carries a 0–1 score, a one-line rationale (on an `errored` row, the plain-prose reason judging broke), the turns it cites, and its assertion's **key** — the behavior's position in the pinned test version, the config entry's index — never the content, which is read from the pinned versions at display time. **Scoring is binary**: a grader's fraction (passed ÷ counted, skipped out of the denominator) is reported for diagnosis and decides nothing; a test passes in a run when every applicable `required` copy fully passes across all its simulations. Overall outcomes are always computed from verdict rows at read time, never stored. Thresholds, weights, and human corrections are designed and deferred — see the grader-redesign spec. Extended 2026-08-07; rewritten 2026-08-14, grader-redesign grilling.
   164	
   165	## The onboarding surface
   166	
   167	**wizard** — the complete terminal experience `npx egma` presents when run bare: its UI, the intelligent work performed by the developer's local coding agent, and the deterministic work performed through the same CLI modules as the headless verbs. It takes a developer from nothing to a running first run. The internal split is not a second customer experience, and the wizard is never a second code path. Clarified 2026-08-09 during the self-hosted phone onboarding grilling; originally added 2026-08-06 ([ADR-0006](docs/adr/0006-onboarding-wizard-drives-the-customers-coding-agent.md)).
   168	
   169	**egma folder** — the `egma/` directory in the customer's repo: project, agent, and connection config; one directory per test suite under `tests/`; a `suite.yaml` carrying that suite's stable ID and mutable name; one markdown file per test inside its suite directory; and one file for the project's mock tools. One repository may contain several suites. A suite directory is only a local path: moving or renaming it changes no product identity or name. Editing `suite.yaml` changes the suite name on push. The folder is committed, never gitignored; nothing secret ever lands in it. The platform remains the store of record — the folder is a working copy.
   170	
   171	**platform binding** — the non-secret platform URL written in `egma/config.yaml` beside the resource identifiers that platform owns. It chooses the platform that receives those identifiers; credentials and a platform-instance identity are never part of the binding. An unbound repository uses hosted egma at `app.egma.ai`. See [ADR-0012](docs/adr/0012-agent-repositories-bind-to-a-platform-url.md).
   172	
   173	**pull / push** — the explicit sync verbs between the egma folder and the platform, on git's model: `pull` writes the platform's current versions into files; `push` uploads and **refuses** when the platform has moved since the last pull. **That refusal is a property of versioned things**: a test earns it, and so do the mock-tool overrides that version with it. A project mock tool is unversioned by decision, so it has no version to have moved — pushing `egma/mock-tools.md` is last-write-wins, and a teammate's edit in between is not detected; the run's snapshot and the answers on the record carry that history instead. Sync is always a verb a developer runs, never a background process — two silently-syncing authoring surfaces are the documented failure (Humanloop's copy-drift).
   174	
   175	## Banned words
   176	
   177	Do not use these — in code, schema, API, docs or UI.
   178	
   179	| Don't use | Why | Use |
   180	|---|---|---|
   181	| `eval`, `evaluation` | Everyone says it, nobody agrees what it points at | nothing — informal prose only |
   182	| `evaluator` | Half the industry means the test, the other half the thing scoring it | `grader` |
   183	| `scorer`, `check` | Borrowed words for the judging job — one word per level | `grader` for the authored logic, `assertion` for one criterion inside it |
   184	| `dimension` | The verdict store's old column name for it — one entity, one word, at every layer including storage | `assertion` |
   185	| `gate` | Considered for the must-pass flag during the grader redesign, not chosen | `required` |
   186	| `built-in grader` | Renamed 2026-08-14 — `predefined` is the word users arrive with (Cekura) | `predefined grader` |
   187	| `metric` *for scoring logic* | A metric measures, a grader judges | `grader` |
   188	| `digital human` | The old name, renamed 2026-08-05 — one entity, one word | `persona` |
   189	| `simulant`, `virtual human`, `synthetic user`, `digital twin` | Considered, not chosen | `persona` |
   190	| `scenario` *as an entity* | It's what a test says, not a thing of its own | a field on `test` |
   191	| `session` *for a conversation* | Same thing as a simulation | `simulation` |
   192	| `trial`, `attempt`, `iteration` | Running a test twice just makes two simulations | `simulation` |
   193	| `call` | Half of them are chats | `simulation` |
   194	| `conversation` | Same thing as a simulation | `simulation` |
   195	| `caller` | Breaks the moment it's a chat | `persona` |
   196	| `result` *as an entity* | A result is "passed" or "failed" — it isn't the recording | `verdict`, or the simulation itself |
   197	| `experiment`, `batch` | Borrowed from a different world | `run` |
   198	| `expected outcome` *as a test field* | Replaced 2026-08-05 — the test's expectations are a list of behaviors, not one paragraph of end state | `expected behaviors` |
   199	| `tool mock` | The inverted form of the entity's name — one entity, one word | `mock tool` |
   200	| `stub`, `fake` *for a mock tool* | Same job, one word | `mock tool` |
   201	
   202	**One carve-out, and it is not a loophole.** `session` **is the right word for a signed-in browser session**, and the ban does not reach it. The auth provider owns a `session` table, the provider seam's fourth method is `revokeSession`, and [ADR-0001](docs/adr/0001-auth-provider-owns-identity-only.md) and the control-plane spec both require the word in that sense — so the unqualified ban forbade what the decision records mandate, which is how a glossary stops being consulted. Added 2026-08-01 after the control-plane code review found the contradiction, with roughly ninety correct uses already in the codebase. The ban stands exactly where it was aimed: **`session` never names a conversation.** A simulation is a simulation.
   203	
   204	The same carve-out covers one more seam, for the same reason: **the Agent Client Protocol names its connection to a driven coding agent a `session`** (`session/new`, `session/prompt`, `session/request_permission` are the wire methods), and [ADR-0006](docs/adr/0006-onboarding-wizard-drives-the-customers-coding-agent.md) mandates that SDK — so the CLI's ACP seam uses the protocol's word as-is, exactly as the auth seam uses the provider's. Added 2026-08-06 after the walking-skeleton code review hit the contradiction. Both carve-outs point the same direction: a `session` is standing machinery you connect to, never the conversation a persona has with an agent.
   205	
   206	## Reserved words
   207	
   208	Good words. Each means exactly one thing and is never borrowed for another.
   209	
   210	| Word | Always means | Never means |
   211	|---|---|---|
   212	| `user` | the developer using egma | the persona |
   213	| `customer` | the organization paying for egma | the persona |
   214	| `agent` | the voice agent under test | egma's side of the call |
   215	| `human` | the caller's side of a transcript | a real person reviewing results |
   216	| `project` | the tenancy container below the organization | any resource inside one — LangSmith's collision, where "project" is a resource four levels beneath a "workspace" container |
   217	| `trace` | one conversation end to end, simulated or real — a storage-layer word that never appears in a UI | a UI-facing name for a simulation |
   218	| `span` | one timed thing inside a trace — a storage-layer word that never appears in a UI | a turn specifically; a turn is one kind of span |
   219	
   220	`trace` and `span` were put on this list by [The unified ClickHouse trace schema](.scratch/first-simulation-path/issues/09-unified-clickhouse-trace-schema.md), which needed a word for a conversation that might not be a simulation: a production trace has no test, no run and no persona, so `simulation` cannot name it. A simulation *is* a trace — one carrying a `run_id`. Recorded here 2026-08-02 after a trace-store code review found the ticket's instruction had never landed in this file.
   221	
   222	`global` was briefly the label over the standing pair (Agents, Graders), added 2026-08-19 by [17 — Group the navigation](.scratch/product-ui/issues/17-group-navigation-under-global-simulations-and-monitoring.md) with its objection recorded: nothing under it was global, and a reader could predict organization-wide settings behind the word. The recorded reopen condition — first-user evidence of the misread — arrived 2026-08-20 as the developer's own first look, and the label was dropped the same day: the pair now sits as an unlabeled cluster above Simulations and Monitoring. The word is free again and means nothing in this product.
   223	
   224	## Mapping to Anthropic's taxonomy
   225	
   226	| Anthropic | egma | Note |
   227	|---|---|---|
   228	| evaluation suite | **test suite** | egma's is a named container, not a saved selector or execution plan |
   229	| task | **test** | |
   230	| trial | **simulation** | |
   231	| *(unnamed)* | **run** | Anthropic leaves this slot empty; 8 of 10 voice vendors call it a run |
   232	| transcript / trajectory | **transcript** | |
   233	| outcome | **outcome** | |
   234	| grader | **grader** | |
   235	| assertion (sometimes called checks) | **assertion** | Same word; one 0-or-1 check inside a grader |
   236	| tracked metrics | **metric** | A field, not an entity |
   237	| agent harness | **agent** + **connection** | Split, because reaching the agent is a first-class problem in voice |
   238	| *(none)* | **persona** | Anthropic's taxonomy has one agent; a voice conversation has two participants |
   239	
   240	## Deferred
   241	
   242	Named here so the boundary is clear; decided elsewhere.
   243	
   244	- **What a grader is made of** was settled 2026-08-07 by the grading effort (`.scratch/grading/spec.md`) and **re-settled 2026-08-14 by the grader redesign** (`.scratch/grader-redesign/spec.md`): a library of definitions, running copies, assertions, binary scoring. Where the two disagree, the redesign wins.
   245	- **Thresholds, weights, filters, custom authoring, human corrections, the `ml_model` and `external` types, and any warn tier** — each designed with a named home and deferred, in the grader-redesign spec's future-work section. Deliberately not sketched anywhere else, so the sketch cannot fork.
   246	- **Classification** — labels that segment without judging: sentiment, topic of a conversation, where it dropped off. A third concept beside measure (a number, automatic) and grader (a verdict, chosen): a label, chosen. Every surveyed vendor ships it; none names it. Deliberately deferred so labels are never wedged into verdicts.
   247	- **Whether a persona behaves like a real caller**, and how egma would claim it does, is not yet specified. It is the credibility floor of the product.
   248	- **Where personas come from.** Research strongly favours grounding them in the customer's own recordings over describing them from demographics.
   249	- **Chain-consistent mock worlds** — bundles that keep `lookup_user` → account → booking data coherent across mock tools (the "John Smith world"). Deliberately deferred: project defaults plus per-test overrides carry v1, and a bundle entity can grow out of them if incoherence actually bites. Named 2026-08-09, mock-tools grilling.

It does not copy the suite name, copy its membership, mint a suite version, or store a membership revision or fingerprint.
